newsitem.title: UK: British character stopped race war, Major says.
newsitem.headline: British character stopped race war, Major says.

text.p: Fears of a race war across Britain have proved unfounded because of the decent and tolerant British character, Prime Minister John Major said on Saturday.
Speaking at a celebration of 50 years of independence for India and Pakistan, Major said there was more work to do in breaking down barriers for blacks and other minorities.
But he said communities had got along better than predicted in the turbulent 1960s.
"Many decent people feared racial tensions -- that there'd be riots, killings and endemic hatred, a trench war between dark and light skinned people," he said.
"But the great trench war between the races never happened."
Major said this was due to the British character.
"It was the British character that won the day -- civil, decent and tolerant," he said.

Major, who must call a national election by May 22, admitted Britain was no racial utopia. Young black men living in south London, where race riots broke out in the ealy 1980s, still did not have the same opportunities as white men from the green and prosperous counties surrounding London.
"But we must try and make it so," he said.
But Keith Vaz, a member of parliament for the opposition Labour Party who is of Asian origin, attacked Major's comments as purely political.
"I deplore the cynical attempt to try and use the dignity of the offices of the High Commissions for India, Pakistan and Bangladesh in support of a party re-election campaign," he said.

Lord Swraj Paul, also a member of Labour and of Indian origin, said: "John Major's government has let down the Asian community in Britain time and time again, thanks to its record of economic failure."
